sub_theme: Materials for Boats: Floating and Sinking

lessons.title: Non-Fiction: How Boats Float
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve information from a non-fiction text about boats.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about boats.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what boats are used for.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about boats and floating.
lessons.independent_task: Children read a non-fiction extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about boats or the sea at home.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve mixed addition and subtraction problems within 20.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving mixed addition/subtraction problems using a boat-loading context.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve mixed problems about loading/unloading a boat with cargo.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record mixed operation fluency — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: Predicting: Will It Float or Sink?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to predict whether an object will float or sink.
success_criteria: I can make a prediction.
I can say why I think that.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a collection of objects and discuss floating/sinking.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model making and recording predictions for a range of objects before testing.
lessons.independent_task: Children predict whether objects will float or sink, recording predictions with reasons.

differentiation.support: Predict with adult support, simple reasoning
differentiation.greater_depth: Give a detailed reason based on material/weight

lessons.assessment_notes: Note prediction and reasoning skill — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Predict if a household object would float or sink.

lessons.title: Writing About Our Floating Test
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences reporting on a simple test.
success_criteria: I can write what I tested.
I can write what happened.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple report sentences: 'I tested the... It floated/sank because...'
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences reporting on an object they tested.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note report writing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Report on a test to your family.

lessons.title: Measuring Mass: Heavy Cargo
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the mass of objects to predict floating/sinking.
success_criteria: I can say which object is heavier.
I can use balance scales to check.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using balance scales to compare mass of objects being tested for floating.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the mass of test objects using balance scales, linking to float/sink results.
key_questions: Does a heavier object always sink?

differentiation.greater_depth: Order 4+ objects by mass and discuss patterns

lessons.assessment_notes: Record mass comparison and early pattern-spotting — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap heaviest/lightest objects and their float/sink results.
lessons.home_link: Compare the weight of two objects at home.

lessons.title: Testing: Float or Sink Investigation
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to carry out a simple test and record results.
success_criteria: I can test an object safely.
I can record if it floated or sank.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model safely testing objects in a water tray, recording results in a table.
lessons.independent_task: Children test their predicted objects in water, recording actual results next to predictions.

differentiation.support: Test with adult support, simple recording

lessons.assessment_notes: Note testing and recording skill, a key working scientifically objective — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Test an object in the bath or sink at home (with permission).

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Boat-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read boat-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read boat words.
I can read a sentence about boats.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending boat-themed words (e.g. 'float', 'sail', 'raft').
lessons.independent_task: Children read boat-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading boat words over the week.

lessons.title: Shapes for Boat Building
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify 2D and 3D shapes suitable for boat building.
success_criteria: I can name shapes used in a boat design.
I can say why a shape is useful.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of boat shapes/hulls.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss which shapes make good boat hulls (wide, flat-bottomed vs pointed) linking to shape names.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify and label shapes in different boat hull designs.
key_questions: Why might this shape float well?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why certain shapes float better

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied to a design context — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Look at the shape of boats in pictures or real life.

lessons.title: Designing a Boat Hull Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to design a boat hull shape based on floating test results.
success_criteria: I can sketch a boat hull design.
I can explain why it should float.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap floating test results from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sketching a boat hull design, applying learning about shape and material.
lessons.independent_task: Children sketch their own boat hull design, labelling why it should float.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain design choices using multiple science concepts

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of floating/material knowledge to design — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Show your boat design to your family and explain it.

lessons.title: Writing Instructions: How to Build a Toy Boat
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple sequenced instructions.
success_criteria: I can write instructions using sequencing words.
I can put steps in order.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple instructions for building a toy boat.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 3-4 step instructions for building a toy boat, using sequencing words.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing and sequencing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share instructions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Write instructions for a simple task at home.

lessons.title: Grouping and Sharing: Boat Crews
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve grouping and sharing problems using a boat crew context.
success_criteria: I can share people equally between boats.
I can group people into equal boat crews.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sharing and grouping from Week 4.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sharing/grouping a number of 'sailors' equally between boats.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve sharing and grouping problems with a boat crew context using counters.
key_questions: How many sailors on each boat if shared fairly?
How many boats needed for crews of 2?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record early multiplication/division understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.

lessons.title: Building and Testing a Toy Boat
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to build a simple toy boat and test if it floats.
success_criteria: I can build a boat using my design.
I can test if it floats.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap boat hull designs from Wednesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss building a simple boat using foil, card or other materials based on designs.
lessons.independent_task: Children build their toy boat and test it in the water tray, noting results.
resources_needed: Foil, card, or other boat-building materials
key_questions: What would you change next time?

differentiation.greater_depth: Improve design after initial test and re-test

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of design and testing skills, a strong SCI.MAT/working scientifically outcome.
lessons.home_link: Build a simple boat with recycled materials at home and test it.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Toy Boats
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their boat design and test results clearly.
success_criteria: I can describe my boat design.
I can explain my test results.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap presenting skills from earlier topics.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a design and its results.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their toy boat and test results to a small group.
key_questions: What happened when you tested it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific reporting progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Present your boat to your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Mixed Operations and Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply addition, subtraction and shape skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can add and subtract within 20.
I can name shapes used in boats.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's mixed operations and shape learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: mixed word problems, shape identification.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 18 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the weekend.

lessons.title: Materials for Boats Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about floating, sinking and materials.
success_criteria: I can say what makes something float.
I can recall our boat test results.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering floating, sinking, and boat design.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Floating and Sinking' display.
key_questions: What was the best material for our boats?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain testing methods and conclusions in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skills progress across the topic — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about floating and sinking with your family.
